name: Rock Sea Lavender
grown_as: William's plant is entered as Limonium britannicum, a Cornish rock sea-lavender of North Cornwall cliffs, one of a group of very similar small species once all called Limonium binervosum. Grown in the rockery in sand.
habit: A low, tough cushion: a rosette of leathery leaves at the base, 10 to 15 cm across, with many wiry, zig-zag branched flowering stems 10 to 30 cm tall.

leaf.arrangement: A rosette at the base; the flowering stems leafless
leaf.outline: Spoon-shaped to narrowly oval, 2 to 6 cm long, widest towards the tip
leaf.base: Tapering into a long narrow winged stalk
leaf.tip: Rounded to blunt, sometimes with a tiny point
leaf.veins: A midrib with a fainter vein either side running up from the base
leaf.stalk: Narrow and winged, merging into the blade

flower.form: A tiny five-petalled flower sitting in a funnel-shaped papery calyx
flower.centre: Tiny; not seen at drawing scale
flower.behind: A small funnel-shaped calyx, papery and pale, with small papery bracts at the base of each flower group
flower.carried: In short, dense, one-sided spikes along the upper side of the branches of the wiry, zig-zag flowering stems; the lowest branches often bare

fruit: The papery calyces stay on the dry branched stems, fading to straw colour, each holding one small, narrow brown seed about 2 mm.
seedling: Two small oval seed leaves, then small spoon-shaped leaves in a rosette
winter: An evergreen rosette of leathery blue-green leaves, often with the old dry flower stems still standing.

leaf: spoon-shaped leaf tapering into a long winged stalk
bloom: tiny pale violet five-petalled flowers in papery calyces
packed in a short one-sided spike along a branch
seed: small narrow brown seeds, often still in a papery calyx
young: a low rosette of leathery spoon-shaped blue-green leaves
flower: a rosette of leathery leaves with many wiry zig-zag branched stems above
short one-sided spikes of lilac flowers along the branches
seedhead: dry branched stems holding straw-coloured papery calyces
dormant: an evergreen rosette of blue-green leaves, old dry stems above

look_alikes: Common sea-lavender (Limonium vulgare) of saltmarshes has bigger, broader leaves with side veins and dense flat-topped heads. Lax-flowered sea-lavender has looser spikes. Statice (Limonium sinuatum) has wavy-lobed leaves and winged stems. Thrift has grass-like leaves and round pink heads.
